This is wild and if schools keep doing this, many parents with resources are gonna pull their kids out. Not everyone will die on the anti-screen hill, but many will (I would, for elementary schoolers especially). There are whole campaigns around “wait till eighth” to give kids a cell phone and then schools demand they get iPads in sixth (or earlier)? This steamrolls parental decision-making. And it will drive some number of families out of public school systems, which is not good.


Heather Barr

Anyway I have zero judgment for the parents who offer limited screen time occasionally and in a pinch. I have a lot of judgment for parents who give their babies or toddlers SEVERAL HOURS of screen time EVERY DAY. 

I also judge you if you hit your kids, give them candy for dinner every night, refuse to ever use a car seat, or smoke cigarettes inside a house you share with them. Some parenting decision are bad and you may have your own reasons for making them, but sometimes judgment is warranted

I am begging people to please read. I didn't say that you're destroying your three-year-old if you put on 20 minutes of Daniel Tiger so you can make dinner, or if they watch two hours of Miss Rachel when the whole family has the stomach flu. 

The tweet says TWO TO THREE HOURS PER DAY. That's not using screentime in a pinch.

Parenting is hard etc but I’m sorry if you’re allowing your toddler 2-3 hours of screen time per day you actually are failing them and you’re failing as a parent. This past week I saw at least a dozen toddlers running around with devices, some with phones clipped to their strollers(!). Your toddler has only been in the world for a short time. It’s still very interesting to them if you let them look up at it.


Camus (@newstart_2024)

I truly think we've made something special. So if this sounds like something you might like, I hope you take the leap and sign up. Full disclosure it's mostly women. Most come alone, some bring a friend. But you can come as you are, whoever you are, with whoever you want to come with.

Retreats are very very very fun and I hope you'll consider joining me! Not to toot my own horn too loudly but ever since my collaborator Emily and I hosted our first retreat together we've had multiple repeat retreaters return on every single retreat, and at this point we've done at least a dozen.

Imagine taking a week to have all of your needs met: someone offering you creative practice, someone offering you movement practice, dinner reservations made, interesting people around the table, wine poured on when you arrive. Space to make and move and be. onthegroundretreats.com/retreat/greece

I host writing and yoga retreats around the world. And no, "go on a yoga retreat" is not the answer to society-wide loneliness or burnout or any Big Huge Problems. But it is one way to give yourself a damn break. To have fun. To exhale. onthegroundretreats.com/retreat/greece

We hear a lot about loneliness epidemics, too much stress, too much time on screens, too little time with other people, too much work and not enough creation. One antidote: Travel to a magical place with a small group of people. Write. Move your body. Make lasting friendships.
